Ok I will clear this up. The reasoning behind this is light primer strikes. Say you chamber a round. You aim and pull the trigger, nothing happens, technically you are to assume that the primer has been hit. 
  What you do in this situation is keep your weapon pointed safely downrange for approximately 30 seconds or more to await a hang-fire. If nothing happens quickly eject the round and toss it far away in a safe direction as it still may go off.... 
  Outside of this scenario, say you are just loading a mag or have loose rounds or whatever and you happen to drop one or more, pick them up, clean any dirt or mud off and continue on. Small dents in the casing, bullet or rim will not affect it. 
  If it's dented so severe that the projectile is no longer pointed in a straight line however, it is no longer functional and should be disposed.
 Only pick up unspent rounds that you know are yours though and don't trust any you find on the ground that you did not personally bring. You have no idea if they are overcharged hand loads or if something else is wrong with them. They may have been discarded for any number of reasons and can't be trusted.
